x: Our latest signing, with the ink still wet on the paper, was Jonathon Dunsford thus starting up another father/son walking relationship. Jonathon finished 9th in this event but one cannot go further without giving due mention to our other walker in this event.
In the Boys 2 miles, Jonathon Dunsford finished a good eleventh of 65 starters. In the Youths 3 miles, Martin Bennett did even better by finishing 8th.
After the stipulated 3 miles, John Hall was first over the line, just pipping Jonathon Dunsford to the post. Third, not far behind would have been Carl Lawton but he still had a lap to go.

Bob Carter was 3rd ahead of last year's winner Bob Whitehead. 5th and 6th positions were filled by the youngsters of the Club Jonathon Dunsford and Stuart Bennett who were told to race between themselves and not against the others.
A fourth by Martin Bennett in the Junior 5 miles and Jonathon Dunsford in the Boys 1¾ miles were the highest we could produce in these races.

On the same evening that John Dunsford was at West London Stadium, competing in the Middlesex 10 km Championship, Mrs. Dunsford took son Jonathon over to the Essex Championships to compete in a boys race (which he won) and ended up competing in a women's 1 mile race.
Jonathon Dunsford finished 4th in the London Vidarians Boys race at Battersea Park on May 5th.
At Bebington, Cheshire, in the English Schools Meeting, Jonathon Dunsford finished a close 3rd in the Junior Boys 3km with a personal best of 14:38.

The afternoon started with a win for Carl Lawton in the 3 kilos, followed up by Len Duquemin winning the 10 kilos. 1,3 and 4 was the result for Belgrave in the under 18 2 kilo event won convincingly by Martin Bennett with Jonathon Dunsford 3rd and Stuart Bennett next home.
First off, in the Boys 3km, was Jonathon Dunsford who finished 3rd. We missed out in the Youth/Junior 5km but we did have two Bennetts and Bob Carter.
Despite no outstanding performances in the Senior 20 km, we did have a win with Jonathon Dunsford in the Boys 1600m in 7:38 and a third with Martyn Bennett 50:00 for the 10 km.

On paper we had an excellent chance of a team place but Martyn Bennett was unable to get over from the 'Lakes' and a couple of others regretfully could not make it. Congratulations however to Jonathon Dunsford on his 2nd placing in the National Boys 2 miles.
The Junior 2 kilos was a Belgrave walkover with Martin Bennett winning from Johnathon Dunsford. Finally we placed 3rd in the 5 kilos with Ray Middleton and Len Evans doing us the honours.

Johnathan Dunsford has been continuing his consistant performances including a win in Eire in an inter-club meeting. Our schoolboys have all succeeded in reaching the All-England Schools meeting, results of which will appear later.
A one point margin gave Belgrave victory over Brighton after they had dominated the early stages. In the Youths, Jonathan Dunsford could not hold the Steyning youngster.
Jonathan Dunsford could only manage 4th in the Intermediate, losing out by one second at the finish. Both Stuart Bennett and Nigel Greaves walked steady races to finish in the top half.

Junior Captain Adrian Cook was first home for the Bels in 7th place but not far behind him came Jonathon Dunsford. We know Jonathon to be a champion walker already and on this showing his services will be sought after as a runner whenever he is available.

…nd the 'Brighton', with Ray Middleton and Dave King being present in both cases However, one man we can't forget - John Dunsford - scored in our third place National 50km and winning 'Brighton', went to Canada to the Vets' Champs, and has given full support throughout the year, but is now recuperati…

The race was won by L.Mockett (Ilford) in 27:17 with 5th place going to John Dunsford in 28:43 and 6th place to Jonathon Dunsford in 29:07. Other Belgrave competitors were 9th S.Sharp 30:12, 11th N.Greaves 30:24 and 13th R.Hall 30:39.
M.Bennett was 10th (15:42.2) and S.Bennett 13th (16:32.6). Jonathon Dunsford placed 2nd in the Youths 2km race.

In a one mile race at Brighton on July 20th Carl Lawton was timed at 6:52 behind Roger Mills (Ilford) 6:28. Shaun Maxwell was 6th in 7:06 and Jonathon Dunsford in his second race of the weekend placed 8th in 7:32.
In the National Youths 2km race at Kirkby Stadium, Liverpool on July 26th, Shaun Maxwell scored a good victory in 9:06.8 with Jonathon Dunsford 5th in 10:35.6.

A great race by Shaun Maxwell gained him the National Youths title over 3 miles in 23:37 ahead of C.Hope (Steyning) 23:40. With Jonathon Dunsford backing up magnificently in 23:43 for 4th, we only needed one more starter to have been up in the medals.
Jonathon Dunsford, who won his last race as a Youth at Chelmsford with only one day left in the age group, is now well capable of keeping up with those twice his age.
In his last race as a Youth, the day before his 17th birthday, Jonathon Dunsford won the Everard Youth Walk at Chelmsford on January 3rd.

In the Middlesex County Championships on 15th May Belgrave Juniors made their mark by filling the first three places in the junior 3km walk. Jonathon Dunsford won in 14:55 with Stuart Bennett only 5 seconds behind in 15:00 and Steve Sharp third in 15:10.

Down from Birmingham University for the weekend, Simon Williamson showed that he was in good shape, beating Peter Gardner. Stuart Bennett and Jonathon Dunsford, on loan from the walking section, gave the Bels a full turn-out and ran well into the bargain.

Sixth was Jonathon Dunsford, 25:47, 11th Nigel Morris, 26:24, and 14th Stuart Bennett, 27:06. Stuart had placed 6th with 46:50 in a LPR 9 kilometre yacht handicap at Blackheath Park three days earlier.
Richard Tanner was the first man to retain a Club Championship in 1977 when he reached the 5 mile mark ahead of Jonathon Dunsford and thus kept his grip on the Junior "Olympic Cup".

Our two Juniors Jonathon Dunsford and Stu' Bennett were together and hadn't been tempted into rushing things. At half way the team had settled down and a points tally showed little between the leading clubs of which we were one.
At the Basildon Festival of Walking, Jonathon Dunsford was our highest placed competitor, finishing 6th in the 5Km. in 24.47 ahead of Dorman 26:07, T.

The event was the Southern 3Km championship won by Lightman (Met WC) in 12:40, although first to cross the line was guest Canadian Marcel Jobin in 12:23.6. Carl Lawton placed 3rd in the championship with 12:45.0 while Jonathon Dunsford 14:05 and Ron Day 14:28 also competed.
